metadata.title: पद्मश्री मुकुंद नायक की अतरंगी कहानी  | Mukund Nayak : Biography of a folk singer | Miss Riya Tirkey
metadata.description:
Padma Shri Mukund Nayak, a distinguished exponent of Jhumar folk songs and dance, has garnered numerous accolades for his significant contributions to promoting and preserving tribal music and art. Beyond his prowess as a songwriter and drummer, Nayak is also recognised for his engagement as a political activist. Notably, he is the first individual from Jharkhand to be honoured with the Sangeet Natak Academy Award for his outstanding work in the realm of folk songs.

In a recent interview with Ria Tirkey, Nayak delved into various aspects of his life, shedding light on his relationships, particularly with women, and his association with Ramdayal Munda, a prominent tribal leader and the vice-chancellor of Ranchi University. The camaraderie between Nayak and Munda was evident in their shared dedication to the cause of tribal culture and art. Despite their collaborative efforts, there were moments of divergence, and Nayak candidly discussed the nuances of their friendship and occasional differences.

The interview serves as a captivating exploration of Mukund Nayak's multifaceted journey, offering insights into his artistic pursuits, political activism, and the dynamics of his relationships, including the one he shared with Ramdayal Munda.
